subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & recommendation for Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.io>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & recommendation for Acme

Hi Sam / Lina —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our demo and the use cases you described (customer support summarization + multi-turn chat assist), I pulled together a short list of model variants I recommend for evaluation along with rationale and tradeoffs. High-level summary below; I attached the prompt set and a short benchmark PDF with throughput/latency/cost numbers for the same test corpus we discussed.

Recommended shortlist (first-pass):
- redwood-2.7b-quant (8-bit) — Best cost/latency balance for high throughput. Good summary quality on short tickets (<= 200 tokens).
- redwood-13b-ptq — Higher quality for preserving nuance and multi-turn context; ~2.5x token cost vs 2.7b but better on hallucination-sensitive prompts.
- open-synth-30b-INT4 — Highest quality for edge cases and long context but higher latency and variability; consider only for prioritized flows.

Tradeoffs & notes:
- Cost vs quality: 2.7b-quant is ~40% of the token cost of the 13b PTQ variant and completes ~2.8x faster at p50 on the same GPU profile. The 13b-ptq materially reduces regression on your top-20 prompts that exercise factuality.
- Latency tail: the 30b INT4 shows higher p95/p99 (see attached PDF). If 99th percentile latency is critical we recommend dedicated capacity + KV cache priming.
- Evaluation plan: run a 48–72 hour A/B run across a representative prompt subset (attached acme_prompt_set_v1.json, ~120 prompts). We'll measure quality (human eval from your SMEs), cost, and failure rates.

Next steps I propose:
1) You opt-in to the 48h evaluation and pick the two variants you want compared (I recommend redwood-2.7b-quant vs redwood-13b-ptq).
2) We spin up a short Dedicated eval with isolated capacity and share a dashboard link (we'll include per-token cost and p50/p95/p99).
3) Dev (cc'd) will scope any prompt engineering / prompt-set tweaks we should apply before the run.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_benchmarks_q2_2026.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the benchmark.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Sam Patel <sam@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.io>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & recommendation for Acme

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. Quick questions: 

- For the 13b-ptq, what's the expected p99 latency on a standard Dedicated instance? We care about p99 for live chat.
- For the 2.7b-quant, do you have any examples in the benchmark where it failed on the top-20 prompts? We can't afford hallucinations on billing-related tickets.
- Are there any limits on tokens/context for the eval runs? We'll need ~4k context for some of our flows.

If that all looks good, we'd be happy to run the 48h eval. Also can we get a short trial credit and a canary window where those requests route to dedicated infra? Lina — can you confirm availability for the eval next week?

Best,
Sam
Head of Product, Acme Corp

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.io>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & recommendation for Acme

Hi Sam — quick answers from infra/eng side: 

- p99 for redwood-13b-ptq on a standard Dedicated m-profile GPU is ~420–520ms for 512-token responses in our tests; with 4k context we see p99 increase to ~900–1200ms depending on KV cache warm state. If p99 must be <500ms we recommend either: (a) keep 13b for non-live-critical flows and use 2.7b for live chat, or (b) use a higher-tier dedicated profile and enable prefix/KV caching + batching.
- On the top-20 prompts: the benchmark PDF flags ~5 prompts where redwood-2.7b-quant produced incomplete facts (mostly in long, multi-sentence invoices). We can scope targeted prompt engineering to reduce those failures — see notes in acme_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt variants 7–12).
- Token limits for eval: we can support 8k context on Dedicated if you pick the 'extended context' option; it increases cost ~1.6x but keeps latency within reason if you provision higher GPU memory. For the initial 48h run we can start with 4k and toggle to 8k if needed.

Michael — can you confirm estimated trial credit and whether we can schedule a canary Dedicated window next Tuesday?

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
